teachingPoint: Removal is documented in detail, by the people who carried it out. The evidence is strong and the title is contested anyway — which is why a provenance score is not a legitimacy score.
explanation:
PROVENANCE CONFIDENCE SCORE: 48/100
The score is built by accumulation, not by deduction. It starts at 30 (the honest baseline for 'nothing is known') and gains credit for authoritative records (+18 each) and press reports (+8 each). Gaps in the early chain, and hits in stolen-art registers, subtract points. An object with no published history scores near 30 — not near 100. Absence of evidence is not evidence of clean provenance.

Score build-up:
  +30 — base score — 'nothing is known' starting position (ADR-002) → running total: 30
  +18 — authority record: "Cast at the Benin royal court, Benin City (present-day Edo State, Nigeria). Commemorative brass plaques were produced by the Igun Eronmwon guild of royal brass-casters under royal commission, depicting court ceremonies, warriors, and historical events. Plaques were mounted on wooden pillars of the Oba's palace." → running total: 48
  +18 — authority record: "British Punitive Expedition, February–March 1897. Following the ambush of a British trade delegation (January 1897), a British naval and military force attacked and sacked Benin City on 18 February 1897. Oba Ovonramwen was deposed. British officers removed an estimated 3,000–5,000 brass plaques, ivory carvings, and other royal objects from the palace compound. Objects were initially distributed among expedition members and later sold through naval auctions and dealers." → running total: 66
  +18 — authority record: "Nigeria gained independence (1960) and the Nigerian government began formal requests for the return of Benin objects. The National Commission for Museums and Monuments (NCMM) was established to coordinate Nigeria's cultural property policy." → running total: 84
  +18 — authority record: "Benin Dialogue Group formed (2010), bringing together European museum directors and representatives of the Nigerian government, the Royal Court of Benin, and the NCMM to negotiate the long-term loan and potential repatriation of Benin objects. Germany committed to repatriation; the first transfers were completed in 2022." → running total: 102
  +8 — press report: "Objects dispersed to European and American museums and private collections through commercial dealers (including W.D. Webster and Th. Bokencamp) and direct transfers. The British Museum acquired its first Benin objects from the expedition in 1897–1898. German collections (Berlin Ethnologisches Museum, then the Museum für Völkerkunde) acquired objects through the same channels." → running total: 110
  +8 — press report: "Germany transferred 512 Benin Bronze objects to Nigeria (December 2022 and subsequent tranches). The Humboldt Forum (Berlin) and 17 other German museums participated. Oba Ewuare II received the objects at the Benin Royal Museum, Benin City." → running total: 118
  -18 — cap at 100 (positive-evidence ceiling) → running total: 100
  -12 — provenance gap (2 undated event(s); no complete chain before earliest record) → running total: 88
  -20 — register hit: "Getty Provenance Index: auction catalogue records for Benin brass objects sold by W.D. Webster (c. 1899–1901) following the 1897 Punitive Expedition" → running total: 68
  -20 — register hit: "significant event: looting (1897 British Punitive Expedition)" → running total: 48

EVIDENCE COVERAGE: STRUCTURALLY-UNCOVERED
No register in this set can systematically name an object of this kind and origin. A quiet result here carries essentially no information about the object — it reflects where the registers look, not what happened. The strongest evidence for material like this is usually physical or archaeological, and this tool cannot see it.
Registers applicable but not identifying (category-level or attention-driven): ICOM Red Lists, Wikidata. Silence from these carries little evidential weight.
7 register(s) cannot structurally hold an object of this type or origin. Their silence says nothing.

WHAT THIS SCORE DOES NOT MEAN:
A high score is not a declaration of clean provenance. It means sourced evidence was found — not that the evidence is complete, not that no problem exists outside what was checked, and not that the object is legally safe to sell or exhibit.
A low score is not an accusation of looting. Under the accumulation model, a low score means evidence was not found — which may mean the documentary record is genuinely thin, or may mean the registers that could have spoken simply do not cover material of this type.
IMPORTANT — structurally uncovered: the registers used here could never have named this object. The score measures the absence of a documentary apparatus, not the object. Do not read it as evidence of anything positive or negative about the object's history.
This score does not assess forgery risk. Whether the image is what it claims to be is a separate question on the same scale — see forgeryRisk.

COMPARABILITY:
This score is comparable only to other structurally uncovered objects. It must not be read against a well-covered Western-market object: the same number means 'nothing was reachable' here and 'a documented gap was found' there.
The score is an ordinal measure within a coverage class, not a universal percentage. Ranking objects from different coverage classes by score is an analytical error equivalent to comparing temperatures in Celsius and Fahrenheit without converting.

RISK FLAGS (6):
  [HIGH] repatriationPrecedent: Timeline cites a repatriation/illicit-excavation event: "Benin Dialogue Group formed (2010), bringing together European museum directors and representatives of the Nigerian government, the Royal Court of Benin, and the NCMM to negotiate the long-term loan and potential repatriation of Benin objects. Germany committed to repatriation; the first transfers were completed in 2022."
  [MEDIUM] lootingSignal: Object history intersects a documented looting/repatriation case.
  [MEDIUM] provenanceGap: Pre-acquisition history is incomplete (2 undated event(s); no documented chain before earliest record).
  [HIGH] registrySignal: Register source describes this object in theft/looting/restitution terms: "Getty Provenance Index: auction catalogue records for Benin brass objects sold by W.D. Webster (c. 1899–1901) following the 1897 Punitive Expedition". Verify against the register itself before relying on it.
  [HIGH] registrySignal: Register source describes this object in theft/looting/restitution terms: "significant event: looting (1897 British Punitive Expedition)". Verify against the register itself before relying on it.
  [LOW] registryCoverageGap: 3 of 9 registers have no public API and were not searched (INTERPOL SWOA, FBI NSAF, Carabinieri TPC among them). Their silence here means nothing — the official searches must be run by hand.

disclosure.public:
Role: Public
Description: Anyone. Sees that the object exists, its confidence score with its coverage class, and that it was notarised — and nothing that could identify or endanger the holder.

Fields visible:
  • public: object identity, title, artist, cultural context, image hash, confidence score, coverage class, and the notarisation proof

Fields withheld:
  • source-community: claim status, custodianship terms, and source-community statements
    Reason: Community-facing fields (claim status, custodianship) are tagged source-community and are not visible to ladder roles. They belong to the community, not the institution.
  • museum: physical dimensions, condition, loan eligibility, risk flags, and forensic scores
    Reason: Requires "museum" access level; this role is at "public" on the disclosure ladder.
  • enforcement: full provenance timeline, registry hits, current location, holder pseudonym, and contact escrow
    Reason: Requires "enforcement" access level; this role is at "public" on the disclosure ladder.
  • owner: holder identity and all fields above
    Reason: Requires "owner" access level; this role is at "public" on the disclosure ladder.
disclosure.source-community:
Role: Source community
Description: A community with an ancestral or territorial connection to the object. Sees the public tier plus claim status, custodianship terms and community statements. Never sees museum or enforcement internals.

Fields visible:
  • public: object identity, title, artist, cultural context, image hash, confidence score, coverage class, and the notarisation proof
  • source-community: claim status, custodianship terms, and source-community statements

Fields withheld:
  • museum: physical dimensions, condition, loan eligibility, risk flags, and forensic scores
    Reason: Source communities have a legitimate interest in cultural claim information but not in institutional or enforcement internals. The orthogonal role model prevents this role from seeing museum or enforcement data regardless of ladder position.
  • enforcement: full provenance timeline, registry hits, current location, holder pseudonym, and contact escrow
    Reason: Source communities have a legitimate interest in cultural claim information but not in institutional or enforcement internals. The orthogonal role model prevents this role from seeing museum or enforcement data regardless of ladder position.
  • owner: holder identity and all fields above
    Reason: Source communities have a legitimate interest in cultural claim information but not in institutional or enforcement internals. The orthogonal role model prevents this role from seeing museum or enforcement data regardless of ladder position.
disclosure.museum:
Role: Museum
Description: An accredited cultural institution. Sees curatorial and condition detail needed to assess a loan or an acquisition.

Fields visible:
  • public: object identity, title, artist, cultural context, image hash, confidence score, coverage class, and the notarisation proof
  • museum: physical dimensions, condition, loan eligibility, risk flags, and forensic scores

Fields withheld:
  • source-community: claim status, custodianship terms, and source-community statements
    Reason: Community-facing fields (claim status, custodianship) are tagged source-community and are not visible to ladder roles. They belong to the community, not the institution.
  • enforcement: full provenance timeline, registry hits, current location, holder pseudonym, and contact escrow
    Reason: Requires "enforcement" access level; this role is at "museum" on the disclosure ladder.
  • owner: holder identity and all fields above
    Reason: Requires "owner" access level; this role is at "museum" on the disclosure ladder.
disclosure.enforcement:
Role: Enforcement
Description: Carabinieri TPC, INTERPOL, or an equivalent authority. Sees the full provenance narrative, register hits and the escrowed contact route to the holder.

Fields visible:
  • public: object identity, title, artist, cultural context, image hash, confidence score, coverage class, and the notarisation proof
  • museum: physical dimensions, condition, loan eligibility, risk flags, and forensic scores
  • enforcement: full provenance timeline, registry hits, current location, holder pseudonym, and contact escrow

Fields withheld:
  • source-community: claim status, custodianship terms, and source-community statements
    Reason: Community-facing fields (claim status, custodianship) are tagged source-community and are not visible to ladder roles. They belong to the community, not the institution.
  • owner: holder identity and all fields above
    Reason: Requires "owner" access level; this role is at "enforcement" on the disclosure ladder.
disclosure.owner:
Role: Owner
Description: The holder of the object, identified only by a pseudonymous key. Sees everything, because it is their own record.

Fields visible:
  • public: object identity, title, artist, cultural context, image hash, confidence score, coverage class, and the notarisation proof
  • source-community: claim status, custodianship terms, and source-community statements
  • museum: physical dimensions, condition, loan eligibility, risk flags, and forensic scores
  • enforcement: full provenance timeline, registry hits, current location, holder pseudonym, and contact escrow
  • owner: holder identity and all fields above

Fields withheld:
  (none — this role sees everything)

routing.reason: Flagged for human review: coverage is structurally-uncovered, so the score of 48 measures the reach of the registers rather than the object — it cannot clear anything automatically. An issuer must not sign this passport until a reviewer approves.
